title: Open the Month with One Bottleneck
teaser: Instead of improving everything at once, identify the point causing the most delay.
full_text: At the start of February, choose one bottleneck slowing your work. Define whether it comes from waiting, approval, missing data, or limited capacity, then select the first small intervention.

title: Record the Evidence Behind a Decision
teaser: It can be hard to remember later why a decision made sense at the time.
full_text: For one important decision today, note two or three pieces of information that supported it. If conditions change, review the assumptions before automatically reversing the decision.

title: Standardize One File-Naming Rule
teaser: A useful archive should help you understand a file before opening it.
full_text: Choose a recurring file type and define a short naming rule that includes date, topic, and version where useful. Start using the same pattern for new files.

title: Put One Expectation in Writing
teaser: Details that seem verbally agreed can still be interpreted differently.
full_text: Write down one important expectation about scope, timing, or responsibility. Keep it concise and make the point requiring agreement easy to identify.

title: Define an Exception Rule for a Routine
teaser: A routine can collapse on busy days if its fallback is never defined.
full_text: For one recurring routine, decide when the normal version is not realistic. Define a smaller acceptable version that can still be completed under those conditions.

title: View One Purchase by Total Cost
teaser: The listed price is not always the full cost of a choice.
full_text: For one planned purchase, include delivery, maintenance, subscription, setup, or time costs where relevant. Avoid comparing options only by the first payment.

title: Close the Week's Open Decisions
teaser: Small unresolved decisions can create invisible mental load.
full_text: List the decisions left open this week and separate them into three groups: can decide now, waiting for information, no longer needed. Close the unnecessary ones and set a review point for the rest.

title: Prepare the Inputs Before Starting
teaser: Searching for missing material after work begins can break momentum.
full_text: For an important upcoming task, verify the needed files, data, access, and approvals in advance. If an input is missing, plan how to obtain it before scheduling the main work.

title: Label the Source of One Important Number
teaser: A number is more useful when its origin and definition are clear.
full_text: For one figure used in a report or decision, record the source, date, and calculation method if relevant. Future comparisons will be safer when the definition stays consistent.

title: Move a Checkpoint Earlier
teaser: Finding an error only at the end can make correction much more expensive.
full_text: Add a small intermediate review to a task in progress. Place it before a step that would be costly or difficult to reverse.

title: Reduce One Permission to the Minimum Needed
teaser: Extra access can add risk even when it feels convenient.
full_text: Review one shared account, folder, or system today. Check whether editing or administrator access can be reduced for anyone who does not need it for their role.

title: Add a Buffer to One Deadline
teaser: A plan built only around the best-case path can be fragile.
full_text: For an upcoming delivery, include time for external dependencies and final checking. Make the buffer visible in the plan rather than treating it as hidden spare time.

title: Turn One Note into an Action
teaser: Capturing a note does not automatically move anything forward.
full_text: Choose one recent note and classify it as an action, decision, or archive item. If it requires action, define the first concrete step and who owns it.

title: Use a Question Instead of an Assumption
teaser: The mind can fill gaps in communication with its own interpretation.
full_text: In one important conversation today, replace a guess about intent with a direct clarifying question. Do not treat your assumption as fact before receiving an answer.

title: Deliberately Drop One Thing at Midmonth
teaser: Carrying every open task forward does not protect capacity.
full_text: As February moves into its second half, review one low-value task and decide whether dropping it entirely is better than postponing it again. Record the reason if you close it.

title: Turn One Repeated Task into a Template
teaser: You do not need to rebuild the same thinking from scratch every time.
full_text: Create a small reusable template for a recurring email, check, or report. Keep it as a starting point rather than a rigid script.

title: Track a Counter-Metric for One Goal
teaser: A success metric can hide unwanted side effects.
full_text: For one goal you monitor, choose a second indicator that would reveal harm early. For example, if speed improves, check whether quality or rework is getting worse.

title: Name the Owner and Backup for One Process
teaser: Critical responsibility should not stay invisible in one person's memory.
full_text: For one important process, identify the primary owner and the person or documentation that could support continuity. Make sure access and core steps can be transferred if needed.

title: Test One Decision with a Small Pilot
teaser: A limited trial can reduce uncertainty before a large commitment.
full_text: If you are considering a change that would be expensive to reverse, design a smaller pilot first. Define what you will measure and what result would make the pilot useful.

title: Give One Piece of Information a Review Date
teaser: Some correct information becomes outdated with time.
full_text: Choose a price, rule, contact detail, or procedure you rely on and decide when it should be checked again. Avoid treating old information as current by default.

title: Read the Week by Results, Not Effort
teaser: Feeling busy and creating meaningful progress are not the same thing.
full_text: At the end of the week, write down the task that consumed the most time and the task that created the most value. Use the difference when planning next week.

title: Reduce Feedback to One Observable Behavior
teaser: Broad criticism can make the required change unclear.
full_text: Take one piece of feedback you are giving or receiving and connect it to a specific observable behavior. Focus on what should continue or change rather than describing personality.

title: Think Through the Restore Path of One Backup
teaser: Creating a backup matters only if recovery is understood.
full_text: For one important dataset, check not only whether a backup exists but how it would actually be restored. Confirm that its date, version, and access information are clear.

title: Separate Decisions from Discussion
teaser: What was discussed and what was decided are not the same record.
full_text: After one meeting today, separate decisions, open questions, and action items. Add an owner and date to each action where possible.

title: Use Past Durations in One Time Estimate
teaser: Repeated optimism can weaken planning accuracy.
full_text: For one recurring task, review a few recent actual durations. Base the next estimate on that observed range instead of intuition alone.

title: Surface One Small Risk Early
teaser: Keeping a risk quiet does not make it easier to solve later.
full_text: Share one small issue that could grow if ignored with the appropriate person. If it is still uncertain, say so clearly and note what signal you are watching.

title: Test Whether One Rule Still Helps
teaser: An old control can become unnecessary when conditions change.
full_text: Choose one procedure or check you perform regularly. Identify the risk it was designed to reduce and decide whether that risk still exists in the same form.

title: Separate Month-End Data from the Decision
teaser: Data describes what happened; deciding what to do next is a separate step.
full_text: Review February by recording the facts first, then write your decisions separately. Do not let a positive or negative feeling replace the measurement itself.

title: Use the Extra Day for Maintenance
teaser: A rare calendar day can be a useful checkpoint for work that is easy to postpone.
full_text: Use February 29 to review an existing system instead of adding a new goal. Verify one backup, account recovery path, renewal date, or long-delayed maintenance item and record the result.
